key_insight: QVal shows that dense supervision signals for long-horizon LLM agents can be evaluated cheaply and more directly, instead of relying only on expensive downstream performance. This helps identify which intermediate-step scoring methods are actually useful before scaling them up.
problem_solved: Long-horizon LLM agents produce very long action trajectories, making outcome-only rewards too sparse to guide learning or assess intermediate decisions. Existing dense supervision signals are often used without a cheap, reliable way to compare their quality.
method: Introduces QVal, a low-cost evaluation framework for dense supervision signals in long-horizon agent trajectories.
Focuses on scoring intermediate steps rather than only final outcomes, enabling better comparison of dense reward/supervision methods.
Provides a practical way to judge signals such as confidence-based scores, self-distillation, and embedding-similarity methods before full training or deployment.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, QVal can reduce wasted compute and experimentation by helping choose better supervision signals early. This is especially valuable for agentic systems where long trajectories make evaluation expensive and noisy.

paper_title: QVal: Cheaply Evaluating Dense Supervision Signals for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
paper_authors: Sergio Hernández-Gutiérrez, Matteo Merler, Ilze Amanda Auzina, Joschka Strüber, Ameya Prabhu
